content:
Aisha: Hey team — customer #C-4721 reporting repeated mid-stream 429s on SSE streaming. They say the stream sometimes cuts after ~30s with a 429 and then their client reconnects and ends up with doubled token accounting. Ticket attached: https://support.example/ticket/C-4721 :eyes:

Aisha: Quick summary from customer: they use short-lived bearer tokens (1m TTL), stream a long response (~120s). They see a 429 sent by our edge, client reconnects with same session id, and they get partial output plus extra billed tokens (billing > expected).

dev_jordan: @Aisha can you paste a minimal repro or logs? Is the 429 coming from rate-limiter or auth-service?

Aisha: Logs they pasted (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-14T18:12:01Z] conn=abcd1234 auth=ok token_expiry=2026-03-14T18:13:00Z
[2026-03-14T18:12:31Z] conn=abcd1234 outgoing: SSE chunk 1 (tokens=512)
[2026-03-14T18:12:59Z] rate-limit: 429 conn=abcd1234 quota_key=acct-555 consumed=12000 limit=12000
[2026-03-14T18:13:00Z] auth: token expired for conn=abcd1234
[2026-03-14T18:13:01Z] conn closed -> client reconnects new_conn=efgh5678 session_id=abcd1234
[2026-03-14T18:13:02Z] new_conn=efgh5678 auth=ok token_expiry=2026-03-14T18:14:00Z
[2026-03-14T18:13:02Z] resumed session abcd1234, replaying from last_event_id=45
[2026-03-14T18:13:10Z] accounting: acct-555 billed_tokens=13024
```
\nAisha: They claim expected billed_tokens ~12000 but got ~13024.

Ivan: Thanks. This looks like interplay of three things: (1) token accounting only increments when chunks are fully acknowledged, (2) 429 terminates the connection, (3) reconnect + resume triggers re-generation/replay leading to duplicate token consumption.

Ivan: Important detail: our quota check currently does a pre-check at request start and also checks mid-stream when thresholds are crossed. If a 429 is returned mid-stream, we don't veto subsequent resume attempts — resume is treated as a new request if token refresh yields a fresh auth header. That can double-charge if the generator replays the same tokens and billing increments are not idempotent.

SRE-Leah: I saw a similar pattern during the november spike. Two immediate fixes: (A) ensure resume is refused if the original session already triggered a quota-exceed condition and (B) make the billing increment idempotent by attaching a session+offset key for each chunk accounting entry.

matt: FYI billing team — can you flag this account while we triage? We'll need to potentially credit the duplicate tokens. @BillingBot please annotate C-4721.

BillingBot: Marked account acct-555 for investigation. Temporary credit request created (ref CR-2026-0314).

dev_jordan: Repro steps I'm going to try locally: create short-lived token (60s), start streaming a 2-minute generation with SSE, inject a 429 at ~58-62s, then reconnect with same session id and fresh token. I'll use curl for a simple repro: 
```
# server side: simulate 429 after 60s
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer SHORT_LIVED" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=xyz" \
  -d '{"prompt":"long output ..."}'
```
Client side: when connection drops, resend with header `X-Redwood-Stream-Session: <session-id>` and new Authorization token.

Aisha: Customer confirms they set `X-Redwood-Stream-Session` to persist session; they expect resume to be idempotent.

Ivan: Two engineering tasks suggested:
1) Runtime: attach an `accounting_id` per SSE chunk and make billing increments idempotent by storing last accounting_id per session. If duplicate chunk arrives with same accounting_id, ignore.
2) Edge/auth: when we return a 429 for quota-exceeded, attach `Retry-After` and `X-Stream-Final: true` to signal clients not to resume. Alternatively, return a 409/410 for sessions that hit quota to explicitly prevent resume.

SRE-Leah: Also consider improving observability: add `x-session-token-count` header emitted periodically that summarizes tokens consumed so customer can reconcile in real-time.

dev_jordan: Quick config patch I can try: on quota-exceed, set response header `X-Stream-Terminated: quota-exceeded` and emit a final SSE event like `event: stream_terminated\ndata: {"reason":"quota-exceeded","consumed":12000}` before closing. That should give clients a reliable signal.

Aisha: Customer asked for a short-term workaround — recommended they extend token TTL beyond expected longest stream or avoid token refresh mid-stream. They said that's not ideal for security.

Ivan: Long-term we should support resumable streams with a server-side cursor that is purely read-only for resume (i.e., resume should not re-run generation). But that's a bigger feature. For now, making accounting idempotent + explicit termination on quota seems low-risk.

matt: From billing perspective, if duplicates occurred we should issue a temporary credit and hold until the engineering fix is deployed. Please capture exact billed tokens and raw event ids for the account.

dev_jordan: I'll spin up a repro and paste clearer logs. If I can reproduce locally, I'll open a patch PR to runtime that adds accounting_id and SRE-Leah's header.

Aisha: Customer is asking for ETA. Any idea how long the mitigation will take?

Ivan: If dev_jordan can reproduce today, patch + review might be 2-3 days, staging deploy 1 day, prod safe-deploy 2 days. So plan ~5-7 business days. We can provide a hotfix that sets `X-Stream-Terminated: quota-exceeded` at the edge immediately (small change) — I'll ping infra to see if we can flip within 24-48h.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered for `edge/fast-fail-quota` branch by Ivan. CI: running.

support-bot: Noted. Customer C-4721 notified that we are investigating and a short-term mitigation is planned.

Aisha: Thanks all. I attached the customer's reproducer and sample client code in the ticket. Will update when dev_jordan posts repro logs.

dev_jordan: Repro done: I got the 429 mid-stream and then a resumed session that re-requested the same generation, resulting in ~1.08x billed tokens. Pushed logs to the ticket and opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6789.

Ivan: Reviewing PR now. If tests pass I'll request fast-track deploy to edge.

matt: Billing — prepare provisional credit for acct-555 (amount: estimate based on duplicate token delta).

Aisha: Closing loop: customer happy we're on it. Will wait for deploy and credit. :thumbsup:
